stage1.impression: A clean night render of a translucent armillary globe on a black drum, set on an empty brown-paved quay with a cut-out block of flats across dark water. Nothing gives it away as a photograph: the sky is a flat saturated blue gradient, the left half is an endless featureless plain fading into fog, the houses are black boxes with uniformly blown white window rectangles, and the plinth is a crushed black hole. The globe's rims glow too weakly to be the event, so a jury would see a generic CG mock-up on a nowhere quay, not a specific, striking work on an Amsterdam canal.

blocking_9: The six rims must be the brightest saturated thing in the frame and each colour (green, orange, violet, red, blue, yellow) identifiable at a glance; now orange and violet are not legible and the blue ring dominates
The setting must read as Amsterdam: gabled canal houses with brick, cornices, window frames and varied warm interiors behind the globe, not a flat black block with identical white panes
No void: the left half (paving into fog under an empty blue sky) needs a far quay, trees, railings or houses so the place has depth and edges
The blackened-steel plinth must read as metal with a lit edge and sheen, not a crushed black cylinder
Paving must read as real Amsterdam klinkers/stone at 1:1 with roughness variation and some wet sheen, not a tiled CG texture
Some sign of life (a parked bicycle, a distant pedestrian) and no floating unexplained light source
The coloured shadow, the concept's second hero, should be a saturated, readable pattern in the foreground, not a pale pastel wash at the frame's edge

defects.what: Rim glow weak (emission 0.03): globe median lum 37, rims thin; orange and violet meridians not identifiable, the blue parallel and violet meridian both read blue
Plinth crushed: median lum 4.1, crush 42%; no metal edge, sheen or patina

House windows flat white emissive rectangles, clip 0.84%, all the same colour and brightness, no frames, curtains or interiors; facade a featureless black box with stepped parapets rather than gables, no brick
Sky a smooth saturated blue gradient (b_median 95 vs r 33) with visible grain and a diagonal light-leak band at upper left; no clouds, no city glow, no skyline
Horizon dissolves into fog: no far quay, trees or buildings on the left; the quay reads as an infinite plain
Paving: uniform repeated rectangular tiles with even mortar lines, no wear, no wetness, lum_range only 19.8 across the foreground
A glowing orb floating in the sky directly above the finial (lum 126): unexplained source, tangent with the globe's top
Coloured shadow pool is a pale pastel ellipse with a hard lit-disc edge, partly off to the right; the spot's pool reads as a projector circle
Bollards are plain cylinders with a plastic red-brown sheen
Water reflects only the windows; the globe's coloured rims are not reflected and the surface is otherwise flat black

changes.problem: The rims, the whole point of the work, barely glow, so the globe reads as a tinted glass ball rather than six lines of coloured light.

evidence.measured: lum_median 37.4, lum_p95 109.9 across the globe; orange and violet meridians indistinct in the 2x crop

change.setting: the globe: the rims' glow (emission strength)
change.to: 0.15, with orange and violet raised a further 1.5x over the others so the six read with equal perceived brightness

changes.expected: Six distinct saturated rings, the brightest coloured things in the frame, with faint glow spill onto the plinth top and paving; faces stay clear.

changes.problem: The camera looks along the quay into an empty fogged plain, so the houses sit at the right edge and the globe has nothing Amsterdam behind it.

evidence.measured: left half of horizon is a featureless fog band; houses only from x 760

change.to: [4.0, -9.0, 1.6] at [-0.5, -2.0, 1.7], 35 mm, so the view crosses the canal at about 35 degrees and the gabled houses fill the background behind and left of the globe

changes.expected: Globe in the left-third with canal and lit gables behind it across the whole width; the sky reduced to a band above the rooflines.

changes.problem: Windows are identical blown white panes, the strongest giveaway of CG in the frame.

evidence.measured: clip_pct 0.84, lum_p95 240.8, all panes the same white

change.setting: the houses across: windows lit, their glow
change.to: 0.3 lit, glow randomised per window 0.15-0.45, colour 2400-3200 K per window, with an interior backplate or curtain gradient behind the glass and window frames/glazing bars on the facade

changes.expected: Warm, varied windows that hold detail, none clipped, reflections in the canal softer and varied.

changes.problem: The blackened-steel plinth is a crushed hole with no edge or sheen.

change.setting: the street lamps / far quay's fill
change.from: 2 x 60 W at 2200 K; fill 0.15 W/m2
change.to: move one street lamp (with a visible pole and lantern) to 3 m camera-left of the plinth at 4.5 m height, 90 W at 2200 K; give the plinth's steel roughness 0.35 with a brownish patina variation so it catches a soft sheen and a lit top edge

changes.expected: Plinth reads as near-black metal with a warm specular band on its side and a bright rim on its top edge.

changes.problem: The sky is a flat saturated blue gradient with a light-leak band, reading as a CG backdrop.

change.to: sky 0.1 with a desaturated blue-grey to warm sodium city glow at the horizon and faint cloud texture; haze 0.006/m so lamps and windows bloom slightly

changes.expected: A dark, low-saturation night sky that recedes behind the rooflines; the globe's colours become the frame's only saturation.

changes.problem: Paving reads as a repeated CG tile with no wear or wetness, and the quay has no reflections of the work.

evidence.measured: lum_range 19.8, even mortar grid in the 2x crop

change.to: Amsterdam brick klinkers in herringbone with per-brick colour and height variation, roughness 0.4-0.8 noise and a few damp patches (roughness 0.15) that pick up the rims and windows; a granite kerb at the water's edge

changes.expected: Foreground with texture and small coloured highlights from the rims; lum_range rises.

changes.problem: The coloured shadow, the work's second image, is a pale pastel ellipse at the frame's edge with a hard lit-disc boundary.

evidence.measured: lum_median 55.5, r 80/g 50/b 35, pastel tints; pool edge a visible circle

change.to: 600 W, 30 deg with a soft edge (blend 0.3), 3200 K, aimed at [0.6, -4.5, 0.0] so the globe's shadow falls toward the camera into the foreground; mount it on a visible mast

changes.expected: A saturated, readable coloured shadow of the six discs on the paving in the lower third, no visible projector circle.

changes.problem: The quay is empty and a light floats unexplained above the finial.

evidence.measured: isolated orb, lum_median 125.6, no pole or fixture

change.setting: small props of the street and lamp placement
change.from: orb above the globe, no props
change.to: remove or reposition the floating lamp onto a canal-lantern pole off the globe's axis; add a parked black bicycle against the railing at right, two distant pedestrians on the far quay, and a moored boat or house-boat silhouette on the canal

changes.expected: Sign of life and scale; nothing tangent to the finial.

out_of_scope.request: Give the houses across the canal real gabled facades (neck and bell gables, brick, cornices, hoisting beams) instead of a flat block with stepped parapets
out_of_scope.why: This is a scene asset change rather than a material or light setting; the card lists only the houses' finish (brick) as changeable, but a jury needs recognisable Amsterdam gables, so it should be modelled

out_of_scope.request: Make the orange and violet meridians more distinct in hue from red and blue
out_of_scope.why: Disc colours are fixed by the card; only glow levels may change (c1)
